title: Nationwide Ground Stop: What We Know and What Could Explain It
bluf: As of about 7pm ET the nationwide ground stop is still in place. The FAA is releasing some flights as its high altitude control centers recover. Officials call it a telecom outage and say they see no sign of an attack. Bloomberg reports the FBI is looking at a software update. The evidence so far leans toward a technical failure, which is how 11 of the 13 big air traffic outages Brief reviewed since 2001 turned out. Three things do not fit neatly yet. Several distant centers lost radios at once. The FAA's new AI routing tool went nationwide three days ago. Its telecom network is also mid handover to a new contractor. No group has claimed it and nothing points to a staged event, but no cause is confirmed yet.
caution: This edition is hours old. Every line carries a time and a status. Expect the official cause to arrive in days, and expect it to shift at least once, as it did in January 2023.
changes: First version of this focus edition.

confirmed.text: The FAA ground stopped every US airport at 3:54pm ET for 'extraordinary circumstances and reasons of safety'. Inbound international flights were handled case by case.
Transportation Secretary Duffy said a communication issue hit the high altitude control centers and FAA technicians were investigating.
DHS Secretary Mullin called it a telecom outage, said there was no indication of a 'nefarious' act, and said every flight was accounted for.
At about 6pm ET the FAA said the stop remains, and flights will be released as the high altitude centers recover.
The FAA expanded its AI routing tool, SMART, to all 22 high altitude centers on November 10. AP says it runs from one site near Washington and only sends recommendations.
The same day, the White House and Transportation Department asked Congress for $30.1 billion more for air traffic equipment.
confirmed.source: View from the Wing; NBC DFW

confirmed.text: Flights to Hawaii and Asia were released from San Francisco while eastbound domestic flights stayed on the ground.

reported.text: Bloomberg reports the FBI is examining whether a software update caused it and does not believe it was a cyberattack. The original article could not be opened.
Law enforcement sources told CNN preliminary reports point away from a cyberattack.
Where it started is disputed. One insider account names the Boston, New York and Chicago centers around 3:15pm. Two outlets say Kansas City Center around 3:30pm.
reported.source: One Mile at a Time; Paddle Your Own Kanoo; LBC

reported.text: The National Weather Service reported nationwide internet and communications problems the same afternoon, then told Reuters radars were normal and only stale web content was showing.
Verizon said its network was normal. AT&T took over as the FAA's prime telecom contractor in August, with Verizon in a supporting role. No AT&T statement was found.
Mullin said there was no link to Microsoft's November 12 email outage, and that investigators are looking at the AI tool.
About 7,000 flights were delayed or cancelled by early evening, and about 3,100 planes were in the air toward US airports when the stop began.
reported.source: Reuters via RTE; Flightradar24 via Fox

claimed.text: A forum poster who says they work in air traffic control claims all East Coast backup radio sites failed at the same time.
claimed.source: Forum post cited by View from the Wing

claimed.text: An unnamed source told the New York Post a software upgrade may be involved. One aggregator says the FAA denied that. Neither is confirmed.
claimed.source: New York Post via View from the Wing; HuggingNews

claimed.text: A message on an airline data feed mentions talk of an eight hour outage.

Commenters claim Mexico City airport stopped too, that bank accounts were hit, and that a big sunspot struck first. None of these was found in reporting. FAA high altitude radio uses very high and ultra high frequencies, which solar flares barely touch.

timeline.event: FAA expands its AI routing tool SMART to all 22 high altitude centers, ahead of the 90 day trial lawmakers asked it to pause.
Microsoft 365 and Outlook start failing in the US. Microsoft later blames failing servers and sees no sign of malicious activity.
timeline.source: PPC Land citing Kentik and Microsoft

timeline.event: Microsoft 365 recovery begins at 6:20am. The White House and Transportation Department send Congress a $30.1 billion air traffic request.
timeline.source: PPC Land; View from the Wing

timeline.event: FAA ground stops Chicago O'Hare and Midway for an 'equipment outage'.
Boston, New York and Chicago Centers and New York Approach lose many radio frequencies and go on alert, per an aviation insider account.
Kansas City Center reports intermittent equipment outages, and the problem spreads center to center, per two outlets.
FAA Command Center advisory: all US airports ground stopped until further notice. Estimated end set at 11pm ET.
Duffy says a communication issue is affecting the high altitude centers. FAA calls it a temporary telecom outage.
Mullin at the White House: no sign of an attack, telecom outage, nothing ruled out, no link to Microsoft, looking at the AI tool.
National Weather Service reports nationwide internet and communications problems, later says radars were normal.
Flights over water released: JFK and Boston to Europe, LAX and SFO to Asia and Hawaii. Nav Canada says its systems are normal.
Bloomberg: the FBI is examining a software update and does not see a cyberattack.
FAA: the stop remains, flights depart as centers recover. About 600 flights diverted, per Cirium.
No full lift time announced. No claim of responsibility found.

hypotheses.name: A technical failure: telecom equipment, network or a bad update
hypotheses.summary: Something inside the FAA's own systems or its telecom network broke, with no one meaning it to. This is the official line and the most common outcome historically.

for.point: FAA, Duffy and Mullin all call it a telecom or communications outage. The FAA status board said equipment outage.
Bloomberg reports the FBI is looking at a software update, and the New York Post's source mentioned a software upgrade.
for.source: Bloomberg via relays; New York Post

for.point: 11 of 13 big air traffic outages since 2001 were technical, vendor or human error. None was a confirmed cyberattack.
Dallas in 2025, Minneapolis in August and Philadelphia in September all lost primary and backup telecom paths together.
GAO warned in September that the rushed overhaul of 11,389 uncoordinated project schedules could cause disruptions. Half the copper lines were still being swapped.
The telecom network switched prime contractor from Verizon to AT&T in August, so it is mid handover.

against.point: Past telecom outages hit one facility at a time. This one hit several distant centers at once, which needs a shared element or a common change.
A forum claim says separate backup radio sites failed together. That is hard to explain with one broken box. Unverified.
against.source: Forum post via View from the Wing

against.point: One aggregator says the FAA denied a software update caused it. Unverified.

unknowns: Which network element or update failed
Whether backups were on the same path
watch: FAA or FBI naming a vendor, update or circuit
An AT&T or other carrier statement

hypotheses.name: A mix: an accident made worse by a recent change
hypotheses.summary: A routine failure collided with something new, such as the AI tool's nationwide rollout three days earlier or the contractor handover, and the backups did not catch it.

for.point: SMART went to all 22 centers on November 10, before the 90 day trial ended and months ahead of the spring 2027 target. Mullin says investigators are looking at it.
SMART is a cloud platform tied into every center, which is a new shared dependency.
In October, 25 Democratic lawmakers asked the FAA to pause the tool over safety testing, and the controllers' union says it had no role in testing.
Recent outages were layered: an old circuit failing while a backup was already cut.

against.point: Every description of SMART calls it advisory only. AP says it sends recommendations from one site and none link it to voice radio, which is what failed.
CNN reportedly found no apparent link to SMART.

unknowns: Whether SMART shares network paths with radio links
What changed on the network this week
watch: Any statement from Air Space Intelligence, which built SMART

hypotheses.name: A cyberattack
hypotheses.summary: A state or criminal group broke into the FAA's systems or its telecom carrier and knocked out radio links.

for.point: Mullin said nothing is ruled out, and failures across several regions at once fit a networked cause.
Iran is openly threatening US officials and aviation sites this month. A CISA led advisory in April said Iran linked hackers disrupted US water, energy and government systems.
Chinese groups have been found hiding in US telecom networks for years (known as Salt Typhoon and Volt Typhoon).
Unclaimed infrastructure attacks hit Europe this month, including supermarket fridge hacks and airline bomb threat waves.

against.point: Mullin and the FAA say no sign of an attack. Bloomberg says the FBI does not believe it was one. CNN's law enforcement sources agree.
No group has claimed it. Hacktivists usually claim fast, though a state may stay quiet.
In past cases where hacking was suspected early, like the 2023 pilot notice outage and CrowdStrike in 2024, the cause was internal error.
Researchers say most hacking claims by pro Iran groups in 2026 were false or overblown.

unknowns: Whether officials would say so this early if it were an attack
watch: A claim with real proof such as internal FAA screenshots
Internet traffic data showing a routing anomaly near 3:15pm

hypotheses.name: Physical sabotage or an insider
hypotheses.summary: Someone cut cables, damaged equipment or misused access on purpose.

for.point: In 2014 a contractor set fire to the Chicago center's telecom room and shut it down for about two weeks. The inspector general found insider defenses weak.
September's Philadelphia outage involved a cut backup fiber, and who cut it is still disputed.
Russia is tied to at least 151 hostile operations in Europe since 2022, including sabotage.
for.source: Moscow Times citing ICCT; Al Jazeera

against.point: No cut, fire or tampering has been reported. In both deliberate cases on record, physical evidence showed up within hours.
Verizon says its network is normal.

unknowns: Whether any site or cable was damaged
watch: Reports of damage at an FAA or carrier site
Questioning of a contractor or employee

hypotheses.name: Staged or allowed to happen (a 'false flag')
hypotheses.summary: The outage was caused or used on purpose, to justify war with Iran, emergency powers or new spending.

for.point: It came the day the White House asked Congress for $30.1 billion for air traffic equipment, and the FAA is seeking about $20 billion more.
Hours earlier Israeli TV reported the US told allies to prepare for renewed war with Iran.
Online, the date, the Simpsons blackout claim and the 'planned crisis' story make many people expect a staged event.

against.point: A staged event to justify war would usually come with early blame on a foreign actor. Officials did the opposite and ruled out an attack within hours.
Funding pressure was already public, and the stop carries a large economic and safety cost for the administration itself.
None of 13 past outages reviewed was later shown to be staged.

unknowns: What the funding request and the Iran messaging lead to next
watch: Officials pivoting to blame a foreign actor without evidence
Emergency powers or war measures justified by the outage

hypothesesNote: The five explanations add up to 100%. The odds are a running estimate from the evidence so far, not a verdict. They will move as facts come in. You weigh it.

connections.title: Iranian threats are already moving US people and planes
connections.status: Documented threats, no link to today shown
connections.link: This week the US pulled tanker planes out of a British base over an Iranian threat. Treasury Secretary Bessent was moved to a military base after Iranian threats. That shows Iran has motive and is already targeting US people and aviation assets. Nothing so far ties Iran to today's outage.

connections.title: US reportedly told allies to prepare for renewed war with Iran
connections.source: Hawar News Agency, citing Israel's Kan
connections.link: Hours before the outage, Israeli TV reported that US Central Command told Israel and Gulf states to get ready for renewed operations against Iran. This cuts two ways. Iran would have reason to hit back preemptively. It is also the backdrop for claims that the outage could be used to justify war.

connections.title: Plot charged against a US air base in England
connections.from: Edition 007 and your Iran dossier, Nov 10 to 13
connections.link: On November 10 the US charged three men tied to the Revolutionary Guards and an Iraqi militia over an alleged van bomb plot against RAF Fairford. It shows Iranian backed networks aiming at aviation targets in the West. It was a physical plot, not a cyber one.

connections.title: Bomb threat waves against European flights and TV stations
connections.link: Early November saw hoax bomb threats against at least 16 European flights, then TV newsrooms, signed 'Mikhail Andropov'. They were cheap disruption aimed at aviation and media. If today's outage turns out deliberate, this is the closest recent pattern. If it is technical, the timing is coincidence.

connections.title: Supermarket fridge hacks across Europe, still unclaimed
connections.link: Unknown hackers shut down supermarket refrigeration controllers in at least seven European countries. The EU called it deliberate. It shows someone is testing attacks on everyday infrastructure. Air traffic radio networks are far better protected than store fridges, so the comparison only goes so far.

connections.title: Microsoft's nationwide Outlook outage the day before
connections.link: This is the link commenters raise most. Microsoft's email outage hit on November 12. Two big outages a day apart feel connected. FAA radio links do not run on Microsoft email, so a link needs a shared cause such as a common network provider or a common attacker. None is shown yet.

connections.title: A new chief for the federal cyber agency
connections.link: The White House picked Palantir's security chief to run CISA, the agency that would lead a cyber investigation. A leadership change at the agency in charge may slow or shape what the public hears about the cause.

connections.title: Fight over Chinese optical parts in US networks
connections.link: Microsoft is lobbying against an expected federal ban on Chinese optical parts used in data centers. Telecom networks, including the ones that carry air traffic voice links, depend on such parts. This is background on supply chain risk, not evidence about today.

connections.title: Nvidia's chief resigned the day before amid a spy inquiry
connections.link: Commenters stack this with the Outlook outage and the ground stop as a week of strange events. There is no known connection between Nvidia's leadership and FAA telecom.

connections.title: North Korea's record crypto theft and the US seizure
connections.link: The US moved to seize $1.2 billion of North Korea's Binance haul on November 12. North Korean hackers have a motive to retaliate, but they usually chase money, not disruption.

connections.title: The 'planned crisis' narrative you starred
connections.link: Corbett grouped stockpiling advice in Europe and Japan with a Pentagon plan for bases to run 90 days off the grid. He added the unexplained E-4B 'Doomsday Plane' flight and called it a setup for a false flag or cyberattack. Today's outage will be read as that crisis arriving. The pieces were real, but none of them points to air traffic radio.

connections.title: The doomsday date and the Simpsons blackout claim
connections.link: Today is the 1960 'doomsday' date and a Friday the 13th. The Simpsons claim points to a blackout on November 17, the day of the national emergency alert test. These make the outage feel scripted to many viewers. The date was picked in 1960 from a population curve, so it carries no information about today.

items.headline: Lawmakers had asked FAA to pause SMART in October
items.summary: More than two dozen members of Congress asked on October 13 for a pause in the Washington area rollout. They asked how SMART was tested in severe weather or equipment outages. The FAA's November 10 update did not answer those questions.
items.assessment: Shows prior concern about SMART under outage conditions. It is not evidence SMART caused a radio failure.

items.headline: SMART built by Boston firm Air Space Intelligence
items.summary: Air Space Intelligence holds a 12 year FAA contract worth up to $875.9 million, awarded June 2026. The FAA was reported in October to be seeking an ownership stake in the company. It is described as cloud based and advisory only.
items.assessment: A cloud data platform tied into all 22 centers is a new shared dependency. Whether it shares network paths with voice radio is unknown.

items.headline: GAO warned FAA rush could cause air traffic disruptions
items.summary: A Sept 14, 2026 GAO report found the FAA has 11,389 separate project schedules that are not integrated. Projects land at the same sites without coordination. As of May 2026 the FAA had replaced 2,560 of 5,170 copper lines with fiber. A 2024 GAO report rated over 75 percent of 138 air traffic systems unsustainable or potentially unsustainable.
items.assessment: Heavy, uncoordinated cutover work at facilities raises the odds of an accidental outage. FAA Administrator Bedford disputed the scheduling finding.

items.headline: FAA telecom network changing prime contractor mid modernization
items.summary: In August 2026 the FAA brought in AT&T as prime contractor for its enterprise network program, known as FENS. Verizon, picked in 2023, moved to a supporting role but still runs core functions. L3Harris runs the legacy telecom program. Bedford said in September that 64 percent of copper had been converted.
items.assessment: Three carriers and a legacy integrator now share the network during a live transition. Handoffs like this are a common source of configuration errors.
items.source: Washington Technology (B2), AOPA (B2), The Star citing Reuters (B2)

items.headline: September Northeast outage involved L3Harris backup fiber
items.summary: In September a smaller East Coast outage was tied to contractor L3Harris switching to a backup fiber line after errors at a Philadelphia facility. Other headlines said a Verizon backup cable was cut and the outage lasted about eight hours. An expert said Friday's failure resembles it.
items.assessment: This is the closest recent precedent and points to telecom routing and redundancy. It also shows how fast a cause was named last time.
items.source: Make Tech Easier; NBC DFW; Cybernews and Fox Business headlines

items.headline: FBI reportedly probing a software update, not an attack
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that the FBI is examining whether a software update triggered the communications failure. Per secondary write ups of that report, the FBI did not believe the outage stemmed from a cyberattack or criminal activity. The update, its vendor and its rollout path were not named. One aggregator says the FAA denied a software update was the cause, but gives no FAA wording.
items.assessment: This is the strongest early pointer toward a technical cause, but the Bloomberg original could not be opened and the FAA denial is unquoted. A bad update pushed to many centers at once would explain simultaneous failures without any attacker.
items.source: Bloomberg (headline only), relayed by Startup Fortune and HuggingNews

items.headline: No hacker group has claimed the outage so far
items.summary: Searches of security and general news found no claim of responsibility as of Friday evening Eastern. That covers pro Iran, pro Russia, pro China and criminal groups. SecurityWeek, the one security outlet with a story, said only that a cyber link was unclear. No coverage was found from The Record, CyberScoop, BleepingComputer or Krebs on Security.
items.assessment: Silence weakens the cyber hypothesis somewhat, since hacktivists usually claim fast. State actors often stay silent though, so absence of a claim does not rule out a state operation.

items.headline: Weather Service reported nationwide comms trouble, then walked it back
items.summary: The National Weather Service website showed nationwide internet and communications problems on Friday. Later the agency told Reuters its radars and radar site were working normally. It said stale content from isolated pages had been circulating and there was no radar outage. No cause was given and no link to the FAA was drawn.
items.assessment: A second federal agency reporting comms trouble the same afternoon is the main sign of a shared cause. The walk back reduces its weight, but the original notice remains unexplained.

items.headline: Microsoft 365 outage the day before, officials see no link
items.summary: Kentik and ThousandEyes data put the start of a Microsoft Exchange Online and Microsoft 365 outage at about 12:30pm Eastern on Thursday, November 12. Recovery began only at 6:20am Eastern on Friday, November 13, and Microsoft still listed it as degraded at 9:56am. Microsoft blamed servers failing health checks and an overwhelmed core process, with a full report still to come. A Microsoft executive said there was no indication of malicious or cyber activity. Mullin said he saw no reason to connect it to the FAA outage.
items.assessment: The Microsoft outage ran into the morning of the FAA event, so the two overlapped on the same day. Nothing ties them together yet, and an email service outage would not explain radio frequency loss at control centers.
items.source: PPC Land (citing Kentik, ThousandEyes, Cloudflare, Microsoft), Northeastern Global News

items.headline: Controller targets cut and funding runs out Dec 11
items.summary: In May 2026 the FAA lowered its certified controller target from 14,633 to 12,563. About 11,000 are certified. The government is funded through Dec 11 under a stopgap passed Sept 1. Controllers worked unpaid in the fall 2025 shutdown, and a brief partial shutdown began around Jan 31, 2026.
items.assessment: Thin staffing slows manual recovery when systems fail. The funding fight gives every side an incentive to frame the outage around money.
items.source: KRDO citing Associated Press (B2), Al Jazeera (B2), GlobalAir (C2)

items.headline: Common Dreams: Democrat demands end to FAA AI air traffic tool
items.summary: In September Rep. Don Beyer called on the FAA to suspend SMART, saying controllers were not consulted or trained. Rep. Pramila Jayapal and the controllers union raised concerns too. Duffy dismissed the criticism on Fox News. The piece cited a controller shortfall of over 1,500.
items.assessment: This sets up the left leaning frame of rushed AI and thin staffing. It becomes more salient after SMART went to all centers three days before the failure.

items.headline: Daily Wire exclusive: Hegseth orders bases off the civilian grid
items.summary: On Sept 30 the Daily Wire reported Hegseth's FORTRESS America plan. It said bases draw about 99% of power from the civilian grid. Hegseth cited cyber and sabotage risks and said the US is not looking for war. The piece ran without outside critics.
items.assessment: This is the original public source for the 90 day plan now cited in blackout claims. It shows the plan's stated rationale before the rumors.

items.headline: Substack tracker maps conspiracy claims meeting a real outage
items.summary: A Substack writer traced a Nov 11 4chan post predicting a staged 90 day cyber shutdown and martial law. He linked it to the Pentagon plan, the Nov 17 alert test, QAnon and financial reset claims. He noted AI made Trump videos tied to crypto pitches. He argued coincidence is not cause.
items.assessment: It is the only source found that names the origin of the current false flag storyline. It is a single unverified account and should be checked.

items.headline: Iranian hardline outlet mocks 'hollow' American power
items.summary: Student News Network (SNN), an outlet linked to the Basij, ran a headline saying America's hollow power surrendered to a communications glitch. Mehr News ran a plain headline on the nationwide halt. Neither page could be opened, so any attack claims inside the text are unknown.
items.assessment: The headline treats the event as a technical failure that shows weakness, not as an attack. That framing cuts against any Iranian interest in claiming credit, though the body text was not read.

baseRates.event: September 11 attacks, first nationwide ground stop
baseRates.cause: Deliberate. Coordinated terrorist hijackings. The FAA closed all US airspace.
baseRates.duration: Airspace closed about two days. Commercial flights began resuming Sept 13.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: Obvious within minutes from the attacks themselves.
baseRates.source: General historical record. No page opened in this pass.

baseRates.event: Chicago Center fire in Aurora, Illinois
baseRates.cause: Deliberate insider sabotage. A contractor employee cut cables and set fire to the telecommunications room. He pleaded guilty and got 12 and a half years.
baseRates.duration: Chicago airports shut for several hours. The center stayed out of service about two weeks. Thousands of flights cancelled.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: Same morning. He was found inside the building with a gas can and knives. The Transportation Department inspector general later found contingency plans and insider threat security insufficient.

baseRates.cause: Technical. A defective network switch that lacked the latest software version.
baseRates.duration: About five hours with no new traffic entering Swiss airspace.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: External investigation published Dec 19, 2022, about six months later.
baseRates.source: Swiss Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (A1)

baseRates.event: FAA NOTAM system failure, nationwide ground stop
baseRates.cause: Human error. Contract staff deleted files while syncing the live and backup databases of the pilot notice system.
baseRates.duration: All domestic departures stopped from 7:30am to 9:00am ET, about 90 minutes.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: FAA blamed a damaged database file on Jan 12. It named contractor file deletion on Jan 19, eight days later. FAA said it found no evidence of a cyberattack or malicious intent.

baseRates.event: UK NATS flight plan system failure
baseRates.cause: Technical. One flight plan held two different beacons with the same code. The main and backup systems both stopped on the same error. NATS called the case one in 15 million.
baseRates.duration: Automatic processing down about six hours, 8:32am to 2:27pm UK time. Cancellations ran for two more days. About 250,000 people affected.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: Preliminary report published Sept 6, nine days later. A Civil Aviation Authority independent review followed.
baseRates.source: ITV News (B2) and Yahoo News Canada (C2)

baseRates.event: CrowdStrike software update crash, global airline groundings
baseRates.cause: Technical. A malformed content update to CrowdStrike's security software crashed Windows machines.
baseRates.duration: Fix pushed 78 minutes after the bad update. Recovery at airlines took days. At least 8.5 million Windows devices hit.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: Vendor identified its own update within hours. Its CEO said it was not a cyberattack about 15 hours after release.

baseRates.event: Newark radar and radio blackout at Philadelphia TRACON
baseRates.cause: Technical. A copper wire burned out.
baseRates.duration: About 90 seconds of lost radar and radio contact. Weeks of reduced Newark capacity followed.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: Reported in the following days. The Transportation Department inspector general opened an audit of the 2024 move of Newark approach control to Philadelphia.

baseRates.cause: Technical. Both the primary and redundant communication links failed. No specific physical cause published in the source.
Not stated by FAA. Primary and main backup frequencies both went down and controllers used an emergency frequency.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: No cause published in the source.

baseRates.event: Dallas TRACON outage, ground stop at DFW and Love Field
baseRates.cause: Technical and vendor failure. Repeated failures of a Frontier data telecom service. FAA said L3Harris failed to make sure backups worked. American Airlines said FAA cited two cut fiber cables.
baseRates.duration: About five hours, plus a second stop under 30 minutes the next morning.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: FAA named the vendors within a day and called it an example of outdated infrastructure.

baseRates.cause: Airline IT issue. American did not name the system or cause. Claims naming outside vendors were unsupported.
baseRates.duration: Reported after 7pm ET and gone from the FAA status page by 8:10pm ET, about an hour.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: No public root cause found in this pass.

baseRates.cause: Telecom equipment outage. FAA said the root cause was not yet known.
baseRates.duration: About 2 hours 15 minutes, from about 2pm to 4:15pm Central.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: Not found by the next morning. No later finding located in this pass.

baseRates.event: Philadelphia TRACON outage, Northeast ground stops
baseRates.cause: Combined. A primary circuit already slated for replacement failed. The backup fiber had been cut about 9:45am by a construction crew. Who caused the cut is disputed among Amtrak, NJ Transit and Verizon.
baseRates.duration: About seven hours of ground stops at Newark, Philadelphia, Teterboro, JFK and LaGuardia. Nearly 4,000 delays nationwide.
baseRates.howCauseWasFound: Same day. Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford named the cable cut within hours.

baseRatesNote: Of 13 major air traffic outages since 2001 in this set, 11 were technical, vendor or human error and 2 were deliberate (9/11 and the 2014 Chicago center arson). None was a confirmed cyberattack. In the deliberate cases, physical evidence made it clear within hours. Technical causes took days to months to pin down, and the January 2023 cause was revised once.

international.what: Toronto's Sing Tao ran a breaking headline that the US halt spread to major Canadian airports. Another Sing Tao headline repeated the report of 22 regional centers. No Nav Canada statement was found, and the pages could not be opened because of URL length.

Infobae ran a live blog saying technicians had not found the origin of the failure. It cited two officials speaking to CNN that early signs did not point to a cyberattack, and said the FBI was monitoring. It reported parts of airspace near Chicago went to 'ATC Zero' and mentioned no Latin American flight impacts.

Canal 9, using EFE, led with officials ruling out terrorism and a cyberattack. It quoted Mullin saying this is not another 9/11 and cited two police sources against a cyberattack. A linked BioBioChile headline said Santiago's airport expected no impact on Chile.

ND+ published a 'what we know and don't' explainer citing radio frequency problems before the announcement. It listed the origin of the failure, duration and hardest hit regions as unknown. No ANAC or Brazilian government comment and no named Brazilian airlines appeared. Jovem Pan, Metropoles and Brasil 247 ran similar headlines.
Publinews ran a straight headline on the nationwide departure halt over air communications failure. Page not opened.

Directorio Cubano gave the FAA advisory time as 20:54 GMT, 3:54pm in Miami and Havana, and said US departures to Cuba were frozen while the order stood. CiberCuba reported Mullin rejected a link to a Microsoft outage the day before. No Cuban government or Cuban state media comment was found.

TASS, relaying AP, called it the third nationwide halt in FAA history, tied to 22 regional centers. Izvestia, Life.ru, OSN and Rambler carried explainers, one headline saying the equipment could not be restored quickly. Izvestia's headline said all civilian flights were banned, which overstates a departures only order. No Russian official comment was found.

Kyiv Independent reported the halt using AP and noted the National Weather Service also reported nationwide communications problems. The article opened did not mention an AI system. Focus, UNIAN, Interfax Ukraine and Ukrainska Pravda carried similar Russian language reports.

Xinhua English ran three short updates quoting Duffy and the FAA advisory with no speculation. On Sina, a verified military blogger called it the third nationwide stop since 9/11 and blamed ground radio failure, posting images of notes citing multiple center frequency outages. FX168 reported nearly 7,900 delays and a White House response.

dpa, in Tagesspiegel, quoted Mullin calling it a precaution with no signs yet of a cyberattack. It relayed a CNN report that some airborne crews had to switch to emergency frequencies. No German government, Lufthansa or Eurocontrol comment appeared.

A business travel outlet warned UK return flights could not leave and disruption could run into the weekend as crews end up out of position. It said the Foreign Office was keeping its US travel advice under review. No NATS comment was found.

RTE said the FAA halted Chicago traffic shortly before the national order. It called this the second nationwide departure stop since 9/11. No Irish Aviation Authority, Aer Lingus or Shannon preclearance details appeared.

A Japanese news blog cited FlightAware at about 7,000 delayed or cancelled flights and Flightradar24 at about 3,100 aircraft inbound when the order hit. It quoted Mullin as saying no possibility was ruled out. No JAL, ANA or Japanese government comment was found.

Newsis, using AP, tied the failure to 22 centers and noted the ongoing upgrade from copper cable to fiber and retirement of old radio systems. It cited Duffy's request for another 30 billion dollars. Seoul Economic Daily headlined that it was a communications failure, not a cyberattack. No Korean Air or transport ministry comment was found.

Hardline SNN mocked American power as hollow, while Mehr ran a neutral headline. A Shahrekhabar aggregator headline cited the New York Times saying US air traffic notices vanished. Opposition outlets Iran International and Radio Farda ran straight reports. No Iranian official comment found.
international.source: SNN, Mehr, Shahrekhabar, Iran International, Radio Farda (headlines)

international.what: Al Jazeera's live blog gave the order time as 3:54pm EST and said technicians were investigating. It carried no cyber, AI or staffing angle. In September 2026 Al Jazeera had covered an earlier FAA outage halting flights to East Coast airports.
State agency SANA ran a Washington datelined wire style report using Reuters and Duffy. It noted the 9/11 and January 2023 precedents and offered no cause beyond the communications problem.
Sabq ran a headline on the US weather service warning its services could be disrupted by communications problems. The Saudi Times asked what is known so far. Neither page was opened.
Fes News and Middle East Business in Dubai ran headlines on a sudden fault paralyzing US aviation. Neither page was opened.
Kursiv in Kazakhstan and Press.lv in Latvia ran Russian language explainers, one calling it a massive aviation communications failure. Neither page was opened.

stateNarratives.claim: Relayed AP that this is only the third nationwide halt in FAA history, caused by communication problems at 22 regional centers. Placed it beside 9/11 and the 2023 computer failure with no hostile cause suggested.
stateNarratives.counterpoint: Matches US official and AP accounts. No Kremlin comment was included. Framing may shift once a cause is named.

stateNarratives.claim: Ran a 'moment by moment' live blog on the halt. Contents could not be read because the URL was too long for the fetch tool.
stateNarratives.counterpoint: Unknown whether it hinted at an attack. Needs a manual check.

stateNarratives.claim: Headline said the US banned all civilian aircraft flights. Body could not be opened.
stateNarratives.counterpoint: The FAA order covered departures only. Aircraft already airborne were allowed to land, per dpa, Xinhua and others.

stateNarratives.claim: Three short updates quoting Duffy's post on X and the FAA advisory on 'extraordinary circumstances'. No comment on cause, staffing, AI, cyber or infrastructure.
stateNarratives.counterpoint: Purely factual relay. No Global Times or CGTN commentary was found, so Beijing's editorial line is not yet visible.

stateNarratives.outlet: Student News Network (SNN, linked to the Basij)
stateNarratives.claim: Headline framed the halt as America's hollow power surrendering to a communications glitch, with video. Body not opened.
stateNarratives.counterpoint: Mockery of weakness, not a causal claim. It implicitly accepts the technical explanation.

stateNarratives.claim: Neutral headline that the US aviation agency ordered a nationwide halt of departing flights. Body not opened.
stateNarratives.counterpoint: No visible attack claim. PressTV, Tasnim, Fars and IRNA coverage was not found.

stateNarratives.claim: Live blog put the order at 3:54pm EST and said technicians were investigating a communications problem. No cyber, AI or political angle.
stateNarratives.counterpoint: Bare early coverage. Matches the FAA advisory time given by Directorio Cubano.

stateNarratives.claim: Wire style report from Washington using Reuters and Duffy. Cause given only as a communications problem across all route centers.
stateNarratives.counterpoint: No editorial framing. Syria's state agency now follows a less hostile line toward Washington than under the previous government.

chatter.gist: The biggest video found, at about 742,000 views and 4,670 comments in two hours. The most liked comments tie the ground stop to a Microsoft outage the day before and today. Many read it as a cyberattack or a sign of coordinated events. Others blame the FAA's new AI system, and many joke about Friday the 13th, Skynet and Die Hard.
commonClaims: First Microsoft, now air traffic: this must be a cyberattack
Our enemies are testing us
AI should never run critical systems
The FAA ordered a stop but says it does not know why
Europe was told to stock up on food a week ago, so this is war
Nvidia's spy scandal, Outlook and now this are linked
Next comes a major blackout

chatter.gist: Commenters point to the FAA's AI powered route system, which one says was expanded to all 22 high altitude centers on November 10. Others blame staff cuts, Microsoft outages or Iran. A few blame Trump, calling it a post midterm tantrum or a show. Some say their bank accounts or work email went down too, which is unverified.
commonClaims: The FAA's new AI system went live everywhere days ago
Microsoft and banking systems are down too
Will Trump blame Iran?
Cabinet members have been moved to military bases
The same people hacked freezers in Europe
A large sunspot hit hours earlier

chatter.gist: Spanish speaking viewers lean harder toward the idea of something staged. Some of the most liked comments ask whether this is a false flag or a self attack to justify the war with Iran. Others link it to the Microsoft outage, the 'great blackout' idea, Agenda 2030 and a Netflix film about a cyberattack. One commenter who says they work for an airline in Mexico says Mexico City airport operations stopped too. Another says a pilot told them the radars went down. Neither claim is verified.
commonClaims: A false flag to justify war in the Middle East
Trump theater to get more money for the Iran war
The Microsoft outage was worldwide
The great blackout has begun
Mexico City airport stopped too (claimed by a self described airline worker)
A pilot said radars went down (secondhand)

chatter.place: PPRuNe (pilots' forum), Rumours and News thread
chatter.mood: Calm, dry humor, skeptical of speculation
chatter.gist: Pilots, controllers and aviation fans mostly avoid calling it an attack. Several say nobody knows until the FAA explains, and one warns that any theory now is speculation. The most repeated suspicion is the FAA's new AI routing tool. Posters share hard details: an FAA advisory giving the reason as a communications failure, Nav Canada saying its systems were normal, and some flights over water still departing.
commonClaims: The new AI routing tool may be to blame (repeated, not shown)
A posted FAA advisory: reason communications failure, flights released as en route centers recover, next update 04:00 UTC
Nav Canada says its systems are normal
Some international flights over water still left JFK, Boston and LAX
Reuters reported a nationwide National Weather Service communications problem the same day
An airline message seen on a flight data feed mentions talk of an eight hour outage (claimed)
A UK controller on night shift says flights to the US for tomorrow will be hit

chatter.place: Hacker News (main thread: FAA Issues National Ground Stop)
chatter.gist: Tech readers mostly assume a radio or radar outage inside the air traffic control network. A minority links it to the new AI planning tool, often as a joke. One commenter floated a possible cyber conflict but said plainly they were guessing.
commonClaims: The FAA advisory wording is too vague
Flight trackers show no departures and long landing queues
Maybe the new AI tool pushed a bad update
Possible cyber conflict, offered with clear uncertainty

chatter.place: Hacker News (second thread linking a Reddit aviation post)

chatter.place: Slashdot (story on FAA AI tool expansion, posted 6am ET same day)
chatter.gist: The story on the SMART AI tool went up hours before the outage. The few comments ask how the system fails and who takes over when it does. Commenters doubt AI can handle surprises like weather or hijackings, and one warns it could be hacked.
commonClaims: Nobody has explained the failure mode of the AI tool
AI cannot reason through unexpected events
A cloud system could be hacked or go down

chatter.place: One Mile at a Time (reader comments)
chatter.gist: Only two comments at capture. One blames the previous presidential administration. The other mocks the competence of current officials.

Current officials are incompetent

chatter.gist: At least eight posts on the outage. Many treat the FAA stop, a weather radar outage and a Microsoft outage as linked and deliberate. The most upvoted post relays a secondhand rumor of a dispute between controllers and the FAA and military units on alert.
commonClaims: The radar and flight outages are a coordinated hit on infrastructure
Controllers are in a dispute with the FAA
Military units were put on alert
1402 days since the last ground stop is a coded signal
A deep state final battle is under way

chatter.place: The Gateway Pundit (article, Disqus comments did not load)
chatter.gist: Posted 5:20pm ET, it pairs a National Weather Service radar outage with the ground stop as a double disruption. It does not claim a shared cause. The less than an hour gap in the headline is not backed by times in the text.

chatter.gist: Straight relay of the FAA order with a developing label. It cites a Canadian air traffic control post blaming an FAA radio outage. No hint of hack or sabotage in the text.

chatterNote: Forums, comment sections and public posts, paraphrased with no usernames. Brief read the YouTube comments and the PPRuNe pilots' forum directly through your browser. This shows mood and the claims in circulation. It is not evidence. Reddit and X were not used.

conspiracies.claim: The ground stop is a staged event, or false flag, meant to build support for a wider war by blaming Russia, China or Iran.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Anonymous posters on 4chan, Telegram channels and conspiracy forums, per a Substack writer who tracked it on Nov 13. No named influencer or outlet was found pushing it by evening. Spread appears limited to fringe spaces so far.
conspiracies.origin: An anonymous 4chan post on Nov 11, 2026 under the title "Black November" predicted a staged cyber shutdown, per the Substack account. The ground stop on Nov 13 gave believers a real event to attach it to.
conspiracies.caseFor: Believers point to a prediction posted two days before the outage. The government has not named a cause. Several centers failed at once, which feels coordinated to many people. Earlier real cases of official deception make people wary of first statements.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: The 4chan post named a Nov 17 date and a 90 day shutdown, not a Friday flight halt. Bloomberg reported the FBI does not believe this was a cyberattack or crime. DHS Secretary Mullin said there was no sign of a hostile act. No government has blamed any foreign state.
conspiracies.unknowns: The root cause. Whether any official will later attribute it to a foreign actor. Who wrote the 4chan post.

conspiracies.claim: The outage fell on the Nov 13, 2026 "doomsday" date from a 1960 scientific paper, so it marks the start of something larger.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Viral explainers and listicles in many languages since October. Seen in Australian, Pakistani, Indian, Spanish, Argentine, Mexican, Brazilian, Turkish, Indonesian and Austrian outlets. No outlet found tying the ground stop itself to the date by evening, but the overlap is obvious.
conspiracies.origin: Heinz von Foerster and two coauthors published a 1960 Science paper titled for Friday, 13 November, 2026. It projected human population reaching infinity on that date. The Conversation republished an explainer on it on Oct 1, 2026 via Gizmodo, and the date went viral.
conspiracies.caseFor: The date matches exactly. It was a Friday the 13th. A rare nationwide halt on that precise day feels like more than chance to many people. The paper came from serious scientists in a top journal.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: The paper was a population growth projection, not a forecast of an event. Its author historian says von Foerster, a former stage magician, used a dramatic title to draw attention. World population fell behind the projection around 1993.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether the date shows up in posts about the ground stop over the weekend. How much the date shaped public fear on Friday.

conspiracies.claim: The Simpsons predicted a "great blackout" in November, and the Nov 17 national emergency alert test is the trigger for it.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Facebook Reels first, then Spanish and Portuguese entertainment sites in Mexico, Colombia and Brazil, and UK outlets. Strong in Latin American and Spanish language media in the US. Fact checking pieces also ran in Brazil and the UK.
conspiracies.origin: The episode "It's a Blunderful Life" aired Nov 19, 2023. Set 60 years ahead, it has Lisa recall a Springfield blackout caused by a storm and a nuclear plant alarm. A Facebook Reel tied it to the FEMA and FCC test and to the UK Be Ready campaign. The Reel also said Nov 17 falls 666 days after the inauguration.
conspiracies.caseFor: The show has a reputation for odd predictions that people remember. The episode is set in November. A real national alert test is set for Nov 17 at 2:20pm Eastern. A real nationwide flight halt four days earlier makes a bigger failure feel plausible.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: The episode is fiction and names neither the US test nor Britain. FEMA says federal law requires a national test at least once every three years. This test will not go to mobile phones and says it is a test. A Brazilian outlet reported that FEMA rejected the blackout link.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether the ground stop gives this claim a second wave before Nov 17. Whether the test runs without glitches.

conspiracies.claim: The Pentagon plan for bases to run 90 days off the grid shows officials know a long blackout or attack is coming.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Began with a Daily Wire exclusive and Fox News documents. ZeroHedge reposted it under a "Doomsday" headline. TheBlaze, IBTimes and AllSides aggregated it. Social posts called it a 90 day blackout plan. Local TV ran explainers in early November to address the rumor.
conspiracies.origin: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced FORTRESS America on Sept 30, 2026 at Quantico. Fox News later reported plan documents. The plan aims for every service to run at least 90 days without outside power, fuel, water or supplies.
conspiracies.caseFor: The plan is real and official. It cites cyber and sabotage threats to the grid. It came in the same weeks as UK and EU household readiness advice. Bases get about 99% of power from the civilian grid, so the shift is large.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Hegseth framed it as long term readiness and said the US is not looking for war. A political scientist quoted by local TV said it prepares for modern threats, not a known event. No timeline or specific threat was given. The plan was public six weeks before the ground stop.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether any classified threat assessment drove the 90 day figure. Whether the ground stop affected military flights or bases.

conspiracies.claim: Governments are issuing synchronized emergency warnings, which signals a coordinated plan or known coming crisis.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Associated with The Corbett Report per the tasking, but no Corbett piece was found or opened. The same pattern argument appears in viral posts linking 72 hour kits to the Pentagon 90 day plan, per an IBTimes related headline.
conspiracies.origin: Several real announcements landed close together. The FEMA and FCC test was announced Sept 16. FORTRESS America came Sept 30. The UK Be Ready campaign launched Oct 22. The EU Preparedness Union Strategy from March 2025 also urges three day readiness.
conspiracies.caseFor: The timing is tight and spans several governments. France, Ireland and the Netherlands promote similar advice, per the UK. People see a pattern when many official voices say prepare at once.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: UK Security Minister Dan Jarvis said Be Ready answers no specific or imminent threat. The US test is legally required on a set cycle. The EU strategy predates the others by more than a year. Each program has its own published rationale.
conspiracies.unknowns: What Corbett actually wrote and when. Whether allied governments share a common threat picture they have not made public.

conspiracies.claim: The FAA's new AI planning system, SMART, caused or contributed to the outage.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Mainstream and tech outlets on Nov 13, including Men's Journal, KRON4, AI Weekly, Techaeris and a blog at kingy.ai. Democratic lawmakers and the controllers union raised safety doubts earlier. Kyiv Independent reports an investigation into a possible link. This is the most widely spread cause narrative found.
conspiracies.origin: SMART, built by Air Space Intelligence under a contract worth up to $875.9 million, began in the Washington area on Sept 21. A Northeast ground stop hit the same day. The FAA expanded SMART to all 22 en route centers on Nov 10, three days before Friday's failure at those centers.
conspiracies.caseFor: Timing is close twice. Over two dozen lawmakers asked for a pause on Oct 9. Rep. Don Beyer said controllers were not consulted or trained. The controllers union said it was left out of design and testing. Mullin reportedly said investigators would look at the AI rollout.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: SMART makes routing and scheduling suggestions that staff review before they reach the Command Center. Controllers keep control of aircraft spacing. The failure was radio and telecom links, which SMART is not described as running. No official has linked the two.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether SMART shares any network or software path with center radios. What the software update under FBI review was. Whether the Kyiv Independent report rests on named sources.

conspiracies.claim: The official story of a telecom outage is hiding a cyberattack or other attack.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Questions from the public to DHS, per Ticker News. Speculation across social platforms reported secondhand. Right wing outlets such as The Gateway Pundit and ZeroHedge stressed the vague "extraordinary circumstances" wording but did not claim an attack in what was opened.
conspiracies.origin: The FAA order cited extraordinary circumstances and safety without detail. It was only the second full halt since 9/11. Officials gave differing tones within hours.
conspiracies.caseFor: Mullin said investigators are not ruling anything out. Several centers lost radios at once. The NSA warned in 2024 that Chinese state hackers had entered US infrastructure networks. The vague first wording invited suspicion.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Mullin said there was no sign of a nefarious attack. Bloomberg reported the FBI does not believe it was a cyberattack or crime. Past Northeast outages traced to cut cables and failed backups.
conspiracies.unknowns: Root cause and whether a full report will be public. Whether the software update came from inside or outside the FAA.

conspiracies.claim: The global Microsoft outage on Nov 12 and the FAA failure on Nov 13 are linked, possibly through AI agents or a common attack.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Northeastern Global News, IVN, Kotaku and the kingy.ai blog all addressed the question on Nov 13. Ticker News said speculation linked the two.
conspiracies.origin: Microsoft 365 failed worldwide on Nov 12, cutting Outlook and Teams for millions. AI tools tied to Microsoft 365 also failed. The FAA halt came the next afternoon.
conspiracies.caseFor: Two major infrastructure failures came on back to back days. Both hit communications. AI tools sit inside both systems in some form.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Microsoft said its issue was technical and not tied to cyber or AI agents. Mullin said he saw no reason to connect the two. The kingy.ai review found no published logs showing a shared cause.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether the FAA uses any Microsoft service on the failed paths. Whether either root cause report will be detailed.

conspiracies.claim: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's resignation the day before signals insider knowledge of an AI related failure or crisis.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: No outlet or post making this link was found or opened. Lead Stories ran a fact check on a quote attributed to Huang, per an aggregator headline that could not be opened. Watch item only.
conspiracies.origin: Nvidia's board announced on Nov 12, 2026 that Huang resigned as CEO and director, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. Reports days earlier said the board was preparing to oust him.
conspiracies.caseFor: The filing gives no reason. The timing sits one day before an outage tied by some to AI. Nvidia is the leading AI chip maker.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: The 8K filing does not mention the FAA, air traffic or government contracts. Earlier reports pointed to a board dispute. SMART's builder is Air Space Intelligence, not Nvidia.
conspiracies.unknowns: The reason for the resignation. What the quote in the Lead Stories check said.

conspiracies.claim: The outage, or a coming bigger one, will be used as a pretext for emergency powers or martial law.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: QAnon style channels and the same 4chan to Telegram path described above, per the Substack tracker. Linked to NESARA and GESARA financial reset claims and to AI made videos of Trump announcing a shutdown tied to crypto pitches.
conspiracies.origin: The QAnon "Ten Days of Darkness" idea dates to 2017. The Nov 11 "Black November" post predicted martial law after a 90 day shutdown.
conspiracies.caseFor: Governments do hold broad emergency authorities. A national flight halt shows how fast normal life can stop. Preparedness programs in the US and UK make the idea feel nearer.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: No emergency declaration was issued with the ground stop. Past dated predictions of this kind, including around January 2021, passed without the forecast event. Some promoters ask followers for crypto or fees.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether any federal emergency order follows. Whether fraud schemes spike around Nov 17.

conspiracies.claim: The outage could serve as a pretext for renewed war with Iran, or was Iranian retaliation.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Only as one of several countries named in the false flag chatter, per the Substack tracker. No outlet on the left or right was found making either version by evening. Watch item.
conspiracies.origin: The US carried out strikes on Iran earlier in 2026, and Iran saw hacking and internet outages then, per TechCrunch in March. The Intercept is suing the Pentagon for casualty figures from what Common Dreams calls the Iran war.
conspiracies.caseFor: Iran has motive after US strikes. Iranian linked hackers have targeted US infrastructure before. Antiwar writers note wars often follow attacks blamed on enemies.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: No official has named Iran. The Ticker News account of Mullin's remarks does not mention Iran. The FBI reportedly sees no cyberattack.
conspiracies.unknowns: Any classified attribution. Whether officials raise Iran in coming days.

conspiracies.claim: The real story is underfunding, staff shortages and rushed privatized AI, not a plot.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Common Dreams, House Democrats on the Transportation Committee and the controllers union, mostly before Nov 13. Futurism called the region's system a tangled mess in September. Common Dreams ran a straight news item on Nov 13 without this framing.
conspiracies.origin: The FAA had about 11,000 certified controllers in April, over 1,500 below target. Politico reported in October the FAA sought a stock warrant in Air Space Intelligence. Transportation Secretary Duffy dismissed Beyer's AI concerns on Fox News.
conspiracies.caseFor: Repeated Northeast failures in 2025 and 2026 traced to cables, backups and frequencies. A federal stake in a vendor raises oversight questions. Lawmakers asked GAO to review SMART.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: No finding ties Friday's failure to staffing or SMART. The administration says SMART supports human controllers rather than replacing them. Old equipment can fail under any staffing level.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether the root cause report names old hardware, a vendor or an update. Whether Congress holds hearings.

conspiracies.claim: The new AI air traffic tool (SMART) caused or triggered the outage.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Hacker News, Slashdot comments, GreatAwakening, social posts described by Techaeris
conspiracies.origin: Timing of the FAA announcement on November 10 that SMART would expand to all 22 high altitude centers, amplified by a CNN analyst remark
conspiracies.caseFor: The expansion was announced three days earlier. Kyiv Independent reports a probe into a possible link. TASS says the FBI is checking a software update.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: The FAA describes SMART as a cloud planning aid that does not handle radio links. The reported failure was frequencies and radar. Social posts misdated the rollout as the day before.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether SMART shares network paths with radio or radar links. What software update, if any, the FBI is checking.

conspiracies.claim: The flight stop, a national weather radar outage and a Microsoft outage are a coordinated attack on infrastructure.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: GreatAwakening, Gateway Pundit framing, some Hacker News speculation
conspiracies.origin: Weather Service notice of a national radar outage on the same afternoon
conspiracies.caseFor: The Weather Service did acknowledge a national radar outage that afternoon. A Microsoft outage was also reported the same day.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Mullin said there was no sign of a cyberattack and that the Microsoft outage played no role. No timestamps tie the radar outage to the flight stop.
conspiracies.unknowns: Exact start time and cause of the radar outage. Whether any shared vendor or network sits under both.

conspiracies.claim: Controllers are in a dispute with the FAA and military units were put on alert.
conspiracies.origin: Secondhand rumor relayed without a source
conspiracies.caseFor: Controller staffing and pay strains have been public all year.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: No outlet opened in this slice reports a dispute or a military alert. The post gives no source.
conspiracies.unknowns: Who started the rumor and whether any military unit changed its alert level.

conspiracies.claim: The 1402 day gap since the last nationwide stop carries a hidden message.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Truth Social post shared on GreatAwakening
conspiracies.caseFor: The count is accurate from January 11, 2023 to November 13, 2026.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Any two dates yield some day count. The post offers no mechanism linking the number to a cause.

conspiracies.claim: A foreign or unknown cyberattack is under way against US air traffic control.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: Hacker News (one hedged comment), GreatAwakening, Spanish language web headlines
conspiracies.origin: Loss of many frequencies at once across several centers
conspiracies.caseFor: Several centers lost radios at about the same time. Mullin did not fully rule out an attack per a Politico headline.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: Mullin said there is no indication yet. TASS reports the FBI said no cyberattack or criminal act.
conspiracies.unknowns: Whether the telecom provider has found a root cause. Whether any group claims it.

conspiracies.claim: It was not truly nationwide and was really a Chicago fault.
conspiracies.origin: Earlier Chicago ground stop for an equipment outage, plus short FAA delay entries
conspiracies.caseFor: Chicago had an earlier local stop. CiberCuba cites FAA data showing a short window and a cut in affected flights to 647.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: The FAA advisory text ordered all airports stopped. Duffy cited issues at all en route centers. The same post body says it was nationwide.
conspiracies.unknowns: Why FAA delay data showed a short window.

conspiracies.claim: Leadership failure is to blame, either the prior administration or current officials.
conspiracies.whereSpreading: One Mile at a Time comments
conspiracies.caseFor: The network has had repeated failures in 2026, including a cut fiber at Philadelphia in September.
conspiracies.caseAgainst: No cause has been published, so blame cannot yet be traced to a decision.
conspiracies.unknowns: Root cause and which contracts or upgrades were involved.

indicators: FAA or FBI naming the software update and vendor would shift odds strongly toward technical.
Bloomberg's FBI report being confirmed by a second outlet would firm up the technical reading; an FBI walk back would reopen cyber.
A CISA emergency directive or joint advisory naming FAA or telecom indicators would shift odds toward cyber.
A claim of responsibility with technical proof, such as screenshots of internal FAA systems, would shift toward cyber. A claim with no proof should not shift much given the record of false claims.
Reports of physical damage, cut cables or fire at an FAA or carrier site would shift toward sabotage, or toward accident as in September.
Arrest or questioning of a contractor or employee would shift toward insider sabotage.
AT&T or another carrier reporting a backbone fault at the same time would shift toward a provider side technical failure.
Similar same day failures in Canadian or European air traffic systems would raise odds of a shared vendor bug or coordinated attack.
An explanation for the Weather Service's nationwide comms notice tying it to the same network would point to a shared upstream cause.
Cloudflare Radar, Kentik or IODA data showing a US routing anomaly at about 3:15pm Eastern would point to a network layer event.
FAA or carrier names a fiber cut or routing error at a contractor: shifts toward technical (or sabotage if deliberate cut).
NWS outage confirmed as simultaneous with FAA loss, on the same carrier: shifts toward a shared telecom failure, away from SMART.
FAA confirms backup radio sites failed at the same moment as primaries: points to a common network layer, raises scrutiny of design and possibly cyber.
FBI or CISA opens a case or issues an advisory: shifts toward cyber or sabotage.
FAA says a software push or configuration change went out Friday afternoon: shifts toward technical, possibly linked to modernization.
Root cause tied to SMART data links: shifts toward technical caused by the AI rollout.
coverageNote: Six researchers swept official statements, aviation trade press, security research, past outages, alternative media across the spectrum, state media and 20+ countries. Brief also read YouTube comments in English and Spanish and the PPRuNe pilots' forum through your browser. Many article pages would not open, so several reported items rest on relays and are graded lower.
gaps: No airline, controllers' union or FAA technicians' union statement found yet
No statement from AT&T, now the FAA's main telecom contractor
Bloomberg's FBI report could not be opened directly
Whether radar also failed and whether backups worked is unconfirmed
No security firm or internet traffic monitor has published analysis yet
Havana, Caracas, Ankara and Pyongyang state media had nothing
Solar flare claim not checked against official space weather logs, though it would not explain VHF radio loss
No fact checks or disinformation lab work on this event yet
